content_of_post_to_comment: Question for writers. How do you build tension in a scene where nobody is fighting ? My whole book turns on a character learning she is allowed to stop. Every version of that scene goes slack. How do you hold a reader when there is no enemy ?
comment: Maybe the tension isn't the absence of an enemy, but the presence of an internal cost. A character learning she is allowed to stop still has to mourn the identity built around never stopping. The conflict shifts from overcoming an obstacle to letting go of a self.
